title: I-DGNN: A Graph Dissimilarity-based Framework for Designing Scalable and Efficient DGNN Accelerators
problem: Dynamic Graph Neural Network (DGNN) execution requires passing each graph snapshot through the entire DGNN pipeline from layer to layer, generating excessive intermediate data and off-chip memory access, even when consecutive snapshots differ only slightly.
motivation: DGNNs are increasingly used for time-evolving graph data, but existing accelerators fail to exploit inter-snapshot similarity, leading to redundant computation and data movement that limits throughput and energy efficiency.
method: I-DGNN proposes a one-pass DGNN computing model that extracts graph update as a chained matrix multiplication between evolving graphs through rigorous mathematical derivation, decoupling inter-snapshot computation from the full DGNN pipeline and expressing it as an independent kernel. A unified accelerator architecture is dynamically configured to support the computation characteristics of this model, providing improved data and pipeline parallelism. A new dataflow and mapping tailored to I-DGNN improves data locality for inter-kernel data across the DGNN pipeline. The framework reduces intermediate data movement across layers.
key_novelty: Reformulating inter-snapshot DGNN computation as a standalone chained matrix multiplication kernel eliminates the need to route evolving graph data through the entire DGNN pipeline, cutting both compute redundancy and off-chip data movement.
contributions: Theoretical one-pass DGNN computing model expressing inter-snapshot updates as chained matrix multiplication, decoupled from the full pipeline
Unified dynamically reconfigurable accelerator architecture supporting the proposed computing model with improved data and pipeline parallelism
New dataflow and mapping for inter-kernel data locality across the DGNN pipeline
65.9-71.1% execution time reduction and 85.9-88.4% energy efficiency improvement vs. state-of-the-art DGNN accelerators

metrics.speedup: 65.9%, 71.1%, 58.8% execution time reduction vs. three state-of-the-art DGNN accelerators
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 88.4%, 87.0%, 85.9% energy efficiency improvement vs. three state-of-the-art DGNN accelerators

primary_theme: one-pass chained matrix multiplication for dynamic GNN acceleration
